subject: EdgeOps trial kickoff: integration playbook & owners
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@edgeops.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeOps trial kickoff: integration playbook & owners

Tara — great conversation today. Quick recap and a proposed playbook for the 4‑week trial we discussed. Please confirm or flag changes.

Goal: validate low‑latency inference (streaming and tool-calling) for EdgeOps’ incident summarization flow and measure cost/latency per 1M tokens.

Success criteria (proposed):
- End‑to‑end 99th percentile latency <= 350ms for streaming token events at 1–4 concurrent sessions
- Token cost under $0.0025/token at production batching profile
- Tool‑call integration (ticket fetch + attachments) exercised with 3 sample incident templates
- No PII retention beyond 24h in trial environment (data residency in us‑west)

Timeline & milestones:
- Week 0 (this week): technical kickoff + SRE constraints (data residency, network allowlist)
- Week 1: SDK integration and sample call flow wired against sandbox API routes
- Week 2: streaming load test + KV/prefix caching tuning
- Week 3: quality evaluation, regression tests against provided prompt set
- Week 4: acceptance demo & mutual action plan signoff

Owners (Redwood / EdgeOps):
- Redwood: Jordan Blake (trial lead) — commercial/PMA, Marissa Cole — SE/technical lead
- EdgeOps: Tara Singh — product sponsor, Rob Chen — DevOps/tech owner, Procurement: Priya Rao

Tech notes & asks for kickoff:
- Confirm the list of allowlisted egress IPs for the sandbox (we'll provide ours).
- Confirm whether streaming will originate from in‑region client or through EdgeOps proxy.
- Share a small set (20) of representative prompts + expected ticket fields for evaluation.

Attachments: edgeops-trial-scope.pdf (trial scope + SOC constraints).

Proposed next steps:
1) Tara to confirm the owners above and any additional constraints by EOD Thu.
2) Jordan/Marissa to schedule a 60m technical workshop for next Tue (agenda in attachment).
3) Marissa to share the onboarding checklist and SDK quickstart.

Thanks — looking forward to getting into the hands of the engineers.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeOps trial kickoff: integration playbook & owners

Thanks Jordan — good summary. We're aligned on the goals; a few items / clarifications from our side:

1) Data residency: sandbox must live in us‑west and logs automatically expire after 24h (no external backups). Can Redwood support this for the trial?
2) Latency: our SLT for pilot is <= 300ms p99 end‑to‑end; can we aim to validate to 300ms (you listed 350ms)?
3) Streaming origin: we'll start with in‑region client streaming, but for full test we'll route through our proxy (adds ~30–40ms). Need to understand impact on batching.
4) Procurement: Priya copied — we'll need the standard trial MSA + a short statement of data handling for our security team. Attaching our SOC2 questionnaire for your SE team to fill (edgeops-soc2-answers.pdf).

Also looping in Rob (DevOps) — Rob, are there any firewall or NAT rules we'll need to add?

Happy to run the technical workshop next Tue — either 11:00–12:00 PT or 2:00–3:00 PT.

Best,
Tara
VP Product, EdgeOps
tara.singh@edgeops.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@edgeops.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeOps trial kickoff: integration playbook & owners

Thanks — quick tech notes ahead of the workshop. I put an actionable checklist in the attachment (redwood-onboarding-checklist.xlsx). Highlights below.

Sandbox compatibility / residency:
- We can provision a US‑WEST sandbox with 24h log retention for the trial; will need your VPC CIDR ranges for allowlisting.

API & SDK integration:
- SDKs: Node, Python (we'll send quickstart snippets).
- API routes we'll exercise: /v1/generate (streaming), /v1/embeddings, /v1/toolcall
- Streaming: uses chunked server‑sent events. SDK exposes a 'stream.on("token", ...)' hook.
- Tool calling: we support a simple webhook pattern where Redwood calls your ticket API (signed HMAC). We'll send a sample mapping config.

Performance tuning / batching:
- Start with batch_size=8 and kv_cache enabled. We'll instrument to recommend batch targets after 1k tokens of baseline traffic.

Security/tooling:
- HMAC keys for toolcall and short‑lived API key for the sandbox (rotated every 12h during trial).

Proposed workshop agenda (60m):
1) Quick architecture + roles (10m)
2) Walk through sample streaming flow + SDK quickstart (20m)
3) Tool calling demo + webhook security (15m)
4) Q&A + next steps (15m)

Attachments: redwood-onboarding-checklist.xlsx

I'll bring a runbook for how we'll run the streaming load test. If Rob can share a small test harness or shell script, that will accelerate Week 2.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Redwood (Jordan): spin up US‑WEST sandbox and provide credentials (rotated API key) ahead of workshop.
- Procurement (Priya): review trial MSA; Jordan will follow up with a short data handling statement.

Workshop: Tue, 18 Jun 2028 at 11:00–12:00 PT (calendar invites to follow). Please confirm if this works.

Notes on p99 target: Tara — we'll target 300ms p99 in the ideal path and document proxy‑added overhead. If we see larger delta during Week 2 we will: 1) enable tighter batching windows, 2) suggest a quantized model variant for cost/latency tradeoffs, 3) fall back to a lower concurrency profile for acceptance tests.
